summary: The Annual Charity Fun Run, held September 17th in Jefferson Park and organized by the non-profit Run for Hope, raised an estimated record $75,000 for underfunded local educational programs. The article covers the 5k race, over 200 volunteers, festivities, and quotes from participants, organizers, and beneficiaries. It also describes how past funds paid for computer labs and a STEM after-school program, the organization's commitment to transparency, and a planned open meeting on allocating this year's funds.
one_line: The Annual Charity Fun Run in Jefferson Park raised a record estimated $75,000 for local education programs, with community volunteers and transparent fund reporting.
key_facts: The Annual Charity Fun Run took place on Saturday, September 17th, along the paths of Jefferson Park.
The fun run is organized by the local non-profit Run for Hope to support underfunded educational programs in the community.
The race route was a 5k, and the event catered to all fitness levels, from seasoned marathoners to families with strollers.
Organizers Julian Karl and Sandra Beck led months of preparation, coordinating with city officials, local businesses, and sponsors.
More than 200 resident volunteers, including high school students, retirees, and local business employees, helped run the event.
Organizers estimated this year's proceeds at around $75,000, described as a record-breaking figure.
Maria Gonzalez, a local businesswoman, participated for her fifth consecutive year; Charlie Spencer was the winner of last year's fun run.
Race day festivities included local bands, vendors, food stalls, a fun zone with face painting and balloon animals, cool-down sessions from local sports teams, and massage tents.
Past funds paid for upgraded computer labs and new learning resources at the local community center.
Principal Angela Ford of Whitman Middle School said the funds helped introduce an after-school program focused on STEM education.
Treasurer James McCarter gave a financial breakdown at the post-run ceremony, and Run for Hope publishes detailed public reports on how every dollar was spent.
Student Lisa Durant said a coding workshop funded by fun run donations opened her eyes to new career possibilities.
In the coming weeks the committee will host an open meeting to discuss allocation of this year's funds, and community members are welcome.
